title: Show-Context Tool Reveals What Claude Code Reads Per Session
summary: Open-source Show-Context tool launches on Hacker News, letting developers visualize exactly which files and data Claude Code accesses during coding sessions.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Open-source Show-Context tool officially launched on Hacker News, providing transparency into Claude Code's file access patterns during coding sessions.
- Developer Bernat Sampera created the utility to help engineers understand which files and data Claude Code reads when generating code suggestions.
- The tool addresses growing demand for visibility into AI coding assistant behavior, especially for teams working with sensitive codebases.


A new open-source tool officially launched on Hacker News today gives developers unprecedented visibility into what[Claude Code](https://emergent.sh/learn/claude-code-review) reads during coding sessions. Show-Context, created by developer Bernat Sampera, addresses a critical gap in AI-assisted development: understanding exactly which files and data an AI coding assistant accesses when generating suggestions.


## What Show-Context Does


The utility provides a session-level audit of Claude Code's context window behavior. When developers use Claude Code to write, debug, or refactor code, the AI reads various files from the project repository to understand context. Show-Context visualizes this process, displaying which files were accessed, when they were read, and how they contributed to the assistant's responses.


This transparency matters for teams working with large codebases or sensitive proprietary code. Without visibility tools, developers cannot know whether their AI assistant inadvertently accessed configuration files, API keys, or unrelated modules during a coding session. Show-Context solves this by creating a readable map of file access patterns.


## Release Date and Availability


The tool officially launched on November 23, 2026, with the GitHub repository going live alongside a Show HN post. The project is open-source and available immediately for developers to integrate into their workflows. Early community response on Hacker News indicates strong interest in context-awareness tools for AI coding assistants.


## Technical Implementation


Show-Context operates as a lightweight layer between the developer's IDE and Claude Code. It intercepts file read operations and logs them with timestamps, then generates visual reports showing the sequence and scope of data access. The tool does not modify Claude Code's behavior or intercept API responses, it simply observes which local files the assistant reads during operation.


Key features include session replay, file dependency graphs, and export options for sharing context maps with team members. Developers can use the tool to debug unexpected AI behavior or verify that sensitive files remain untouched during routine coding tasks.


## Why Context Visibility Matters


As AI coding assistants become standard development tools, understanding their data access patterns grows more critical. Claude Code and similar tools read repository contents to provide intelligent suggestions, but this process remains opaque to most users. Without visibility, developers cannot audit whether assistants respect intended scope boundaries or accidentally leak context between unrelated projects.


Show-Context represents a category of emerging developer utilities focused on AI transparency. Similar tools exist for token usage tracking and prompt engineering, but file-level access monitoring fills a distinct need for security-conscious teams and enterprises evaluating AI coding assistants.


## What This Means


The launch of Show-Context signals growing maturity in the AI-assisted development ecosystem. As organizations adopt tools like Claude Code at scale, they demand transparency and auditability alongside productivity gains. Third-party utilities that provide visibility into AI behavior will become essential components of enterprise development workflows, particularly in regulated industries where code access patterns must be documented. For individual developers, tools like Show-Context offer peace of mind that their AI assistants operate within expected boundaries.
